source-integrity.provenance: issuer Q2 and SEC 10-Q anchor operating/financial claims; independent market source anchors current valuation
source-integrity.freshness: Q2 primary evidence July 30; market valuation September 21
source-integrity.duplicateOriginCollapse: issuer and SEC overlap is not treated as independent corroboration
source-integrity.sourceIndependence: market valuation is separate from issuer operating claims
source-integrity.rawDerivedConsistency: raised guidance and large-load opportunity are retained alongside modest Q2 operating-EPS decline and capital/affordability constraints

company-underwriting.financialOperatingTrajectory: Regulated utility earnings base remains profitable; Q2 revenue was about $5.45B and current evidence supports raised full-year guidance despite modest Q2 operating-EPS decline.
company-underwriting.balanceSheet: Large grid/generation buildout is capital intensive and requires debt/equity funding, but regulated cost recovery supports financing capacity subject to credit and affordability constraints.
company-underwriting.customersContracts: Large-load/data-center demand creates substantial prospective grid investment; realization depends on interconnection, generation, permitting and customer commitment quality.
company-underwriting.governanceCapitalAllocation: Capital program is aligned with observable load growth, while regulatory recovery and financing discipline are central tests.
company-underwriting.pricingPowerConcentration: Regulated rate recovery provides structured economic capture rather than unconstrained pricing; affordability limits upside.
company-underwriting.catalysts: Large-load conversion, transmission/generation approvals, rate-base additions and continued guidance execution.

thesisQuality.basis: Essential regulated grid assets, rising large-load demand and visible rate-base investment support durable demand and value capture.

financialOperatingMomentum.basis: Profitable regulated operations and raised guidance are strong, tempered by modest Q2 operating-EPS decline and heavy capital needs.

marketValuationOpportunity.basis: September market data show about 17.5x forward earnings and $65B market cap, a reasonable but not distressed valuation for regulated growth.

catalystScore.basis: Large-load commitments, grid investment approvals and rate-base deployment provide multiple identifiable multi-year catalysts.

governancePower.basis: Regulated capital allocation is disciplined by commissions and observable guidance, though execution across a very large buildout remains material.

alignment2036.basis: Electric transmission, distribution and generation are foundational infrastructure for electrification, industry and compute demand.

crossDivisionLeverage.basis: Generation, transmission and distribution assets serve residential, industrial and data-center demand across multiple states.

bottleneckControl.basis: AEP controls regulated grid infrastructure and interconnection pathways in high-growth territories where transmission/generation capacity is a real constraint.

scenarioRobustness.basis: Essential utility demand and geographic/customer breadth are robust, while rate, load-growth and financing scenarios still matter.

substitutionResilience.basis: Regulated wires and grid interconnection are difficult to bypass at scale even when generation technologies change.

supplyChainResilience.basis: Scale and diversified infrastructure provide planning flexibility, but turbines, transformers and permitting remain meaningful successor bottlenecks.

pricingPower.basis: Approved rate-base returns and cost recovery provide structured value capture, constrained by affordability and regulatory review.

riskEvidence.basis: Capital intensity, funding costs, regulatory recovery, affordability and load-conversion risk are material but moderated by regulated essential infrastructure and diversified demand.

dataConfidenceEvidence.basis: Current SEC/issuer financial and load evidence plus current market valuation cover all required factors; customer-level firmness of the full load pipeline remains partly undisclosed.

scoreRecord.thesis: AEP controls essential regulated grid infrastructure in territories seeing unusually strong load growth, creating a long-duration rate-base growth path if contracted demand converts and regulators permit timely recovery.
scoreRecord.keyRisk: Capital can be deployed ahead of realized load or at unfavorable financing cost while affordability/regulatory constraints delay recovery.
scoreRecord.nextCatalyst: Further conversion of large-load commitments into approved transmission/generation projects and updated earnings/capital guidance.

contradictions.claim: Raised full-year guidance despite modest Q2 operating-EPS decline.
contradictions.resolution: Not material: forward growth depends on capital/load conversion rather than one-quarter momentum; both facts remain explicit.

unknowns.item: Customer-by-customer firmness, cancellation protection and exact financing mix for the full large-load pipeline remain incompletely disclosed.
